newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's exiled king gets back citizenship.
newsitem.headline: Romania's exiled king gets back citizenship.

text.p: Romania's new centrist government on Friday restored the citizenship of exiled King Michael in what it described as an act of reparation nearly 50 years after he was exiles by communists.

The repeal of a 1948 decree stripping Michael of his citizenship was "a necessary measure of reparation, in full accordance with the Constitution which says citizenship cannot be withdrawn from anyone acquiring it through birth," a government statement said.
Michael, 75, was dethroned and forced into exile in 1947 by Moscow-backed communists who seized power after Soviet troops occupied Romania at the close of World War Two.
"We are extremely pleased and hope the Romanian people are as well," a spokeswoman for the king told Reuters by telephone from his residence at Versoix, near the Swiss city of Geneva.

Michael has denied Romanian press reports that he is about to return to his homeland. He was feted by hundreds of thousands of well-wishers during a brief emotional Orthodox Easter homecoming in 1992.
But his subsequent attempts to return were thwarted by the former leftist government and by ex-President Ion Iliescu who insisted that he must first abandon all claims to the throne.
The government's decision coincided with a visit to Romania by French President Jacques Chirac, the biggest defender of Romania's interests in NATO and the European Union.
It followed a promise by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea earlier this month to consider an appeal by monarchists and academics to restore Michael's rights as a Romanian citizen.
The government statement said the restoration of the king's citizenship would have no bearing on the 1991 post-communist constitution which defines the Balkan country as a republic.
